newsitem.title: USA: Georgia-Pacific results hurt by low prices.
newsitem.headline: Georgia-Pacific results hurt by low prices.

text.p: Georgia-Pacific Corp said on Thursday that profits for its pulp and paper business were hurt by a collapse in prices for most products.
Georgia-Pacific reported 1996 earnings of $1.78 a share, before an extraordinary item, compared to $11.29 a share in 1995. Total company operating profit was $914 million versus $2.29 billion.
The company's pulp and paper business reported 1996 operating profits of $390 million compared with profits of $1.6 billion in 1995.
It said it expects the other half of its pretax earnings improvement to come from investments in information systems, and efficiencies and cost savings in our distribution business.

Georgia-Pacific said its distribution business is implementing an aggressive plan to reduce its overhead costs, tighten control of all expenses, operate more efficiently, and increase sales and margins.
Georgia-Pacific will reduce its capital investing to a level that approximates our depreciation cost and use excess cash flow to reduce debt.
Georgia-Pacific said that once it has reached its target debt level of $5.5 billion, it anticipate returning cash to its shareholders through repurchase of the company's common stock.
Total debt, including the accounts receivable sale program, was $5.9 billion as of December 31, 1996, up slightly compared with the $5.8 billion reported at the end of the 1996 third quarter.
Georgia-Pacific's building products business reported profits of $516 million versus 1995 profits of $669 million.
The building products business was hurt by reduced profits in structural panels, resulting primarily from excess capacity and lower prices for oriented strand board.
The company said that it has already identified and implemented half its goal of improving annual pretax earnings by $400 million.
